title: Add release dry-run workflow, lightweight lint-prober runner, and dependency impact scanner
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Release windows have been a recurring source of risk — releases usually exercise cross-repo hooks (changelogs, tag signing, and artifact promotion) but we lacked a reliable preflight to validate those steps and the telemetry emitted during a release. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: (1) a release-dryrun workflow that performs a full non-mutating rehearsal of release steps in CI and emits structured telemetry; (2) a lightweight lint-prober runner that can execute a minimal subset of presubmit linters quickly on changed files (target fast feedback for large monorepo touchpoints); and (3) a dependency impact scanner that maps changed dependency versions to a quick-risk score for release gating. Motivation: reduce release surprises, shorten the pre-merge feedback loop for lint failures on large changes, and flag high-risk dependency bumps before rollout. Changes are intentionally additive and gated behind a feature flag in repo config so rollout is gradual. Checklist: - [x] Add release-dryrun workflow with non-destructive mode and artifact stubbing - [x] Emit structured telemetry to ci/release-telemetry v2 (events: dryrun.start, step.finish, manifest.diff) - [x] Implement lint-prober binary + quick rules file selector - [x] Add dep-impact scanner script with mapping table -> risk score - [x] Wire presubmit to optionally call lint-prober when change set > 200 files - [x] Unit tests for scanner heuristics and runner integration smoke tests - [x] Docs and runbook updates for on-call during dry-run rollouts Migration & rollout notes: - The release-dryrun workflow is opt-in via .github/release-config.yaml -> dryrun.enabled: true. Start by enabling for a small set of repos for one week. - Lint-prober is enabled by default for PRs touching >200 files and can be disabled using PR label ci/skip-prober. - Dep-impact scanner risk thresholds are tunable; default: score>=7 => block release; score 4-6 => warn. Monitoring: dashboards added under Console -> CI -> Release Dryruns and a new alert ci.release-dryrun.fail-rate > 0.5%/day. Why not use existing presubmit? Existing presubmit is heavy; lint-prober purposefully trades coverage for speed by running targeted rules and sampling heavy linters. Related: ENG-1423 (presubmit scaleback efforts), SUP-4121 (customer incident that motivated release rehearsals).

review_comments: Lina Gomez (2026-02-05): Can we ensure the release-dryrun never touches the real packaging registry? Tech review: add strict artifact stubbing and a dryrun-mode env var — CI job should fail if stubbing is not available.
Ava Chen (2026-02-05): Reply: added explicit artifact stubbing step and an assertion that fails the job if stubs are absent. Updated docs to call this out.
Trevor Malik (2026-02-06): The lint-prober selector seems to use a hard 200 file threshold; can we make that configurable per-team? Also request: expose a short metrics tag for slow-prober runs.
Ava Chen (2026-02-06): Reply: made threshold configurable in .github/release-config.yaml under prober.file_threshold and added metrics prober.duration_ms with team tag.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-07): Dep scanner: what's the source of baseline_vendors.csv and how often should it be refreshed? Concern about false positives on transitive minor bumps.

Ava Chen (2026-02-07): Reply: baseline_vendors.csv is generated from open-source vulnerability feeds + our historical rollout telemetry. Added a small refresh job and a note in docs that transitive bumps are scored lower by default.
Lina Gomez (2026-02-08): Approve after CI green and a small nit on emitter log verbosity
